questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Negate a past wish

stimulus.body: En una nota de trabajo sobre este punto se lee: «Ojala no hubiera llovido.» « s log, which form expresses » La nota ofrece cuatro afirmaciones posibles; solo una se desprende de lo que el texto dice realmente.

questions.stem: Con «Negate a past wish / Ojala plus pluperfect subjunctive. / The pluperfect subjunctive» presente, ¿qué respuesta se desprende de la nota?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: a past wish with negation uses ojala plus the pluperfect subjunctive: 'Ojala no hubiera llovido. On that basis "Ojala no hubiera llovido" is the supported choice. Option A ("Ojala no llueva") fails because it uses present subjunctive instead; Option B ("Ojala no llovio") fails because it uses indicative instead of subjunctive; Option C ("Ojala no llovera") fails because it uses imperfect subjunctive instead.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Identify both forms in a clause

stimulus.body: The log note: 'Dudaba que hubiera / hubiese visto la estrella.' Both forms appear as alternatives.

questions.stem: In the astronomer's log, which two forms are the pluperfect subjunctives of 'ver' for 'el'?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: the two pluperfect subjunctive forms for 'el' of ver are 'hubiera visto' and 'hubiese visto. On that basis "hubiera visto and hubiese visto" is the supported choice. Option D ("vea and viera") fails because it gives present/imperfect subjunctive instead; Option B ("habia visto and habria visto") fails because it confuses subjunctive with indicative/conditional; Option C ("vio and veia") fails because it confuses with indicative past.
